newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: MORE TREATED OVER FOOD POISONING OVERNIGHT
More people have been treated in hospital overnight following a food poisoning outbreak in Melbourne's south eastern suburbs, taking the toll to almost 300.
An extra 30 patients were treated at Monash Medical Centre overnight, half of them children, while at Dandenong Hospital, 26 patients were treated for gastroenteritis.
That means 299 people have been treated by the two hospitals since Saturday night, in a scare linked to the sale of Vietnamese Pork rolls sold at a Sprinvale bakery.
The health department says cultural differences are partly responsible for the food outbreak, with many customers and the owners having different views of food storage.
CALL FOR TAX BREAKS TO EXTEND TO MINING INDUSTRY
The Chamber of Mines and Energy is calling on the federal government to extend tax breaks for small business to the mining industry.
The Chamber's chief economist in Western Australia, Steve Gerhardy, says fringe benefits tax changes announced yesterday will be of marginal aid to smaller operators and service industries.
He says the Federal Government has virtually ignored the mining sector by focusing on issues such as parking and taxi travel.
These will no longer attract the same level of fringe benefits tax.
Mr Gerhardy says mining companies are being discriminated against by paying FBT on essential services such as health and housing.
FISCHER TO TRAVEL TO NORTH QLD
The Federal Government has confirmed its offering three dollars for every one dollar provided by the Queensland Government, in relief for cyclone-ravaged north Queensland.
Deputy Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, will travel to North Queensland this morning to inspect damage associated with Tropical Cyclone Justin.
He says he and other Coalition M-P's will visit Townsville and Ingham for briefings on the extent of damage.
BOND UNI TURNS DOWN KENNETT OFFER
Queensland's Bond University says there is no chance it will move from the Gold Coast, despite a generous relocation offer from the Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett.
The university's Vice-Chancellor, Raoul Mortley says the offer is flattering and the feasibility of establishing a branch campus in Victoria will be looked at.
Professor Mortley says the Queensland government has never expressed the same level of confidence in the university that Victoria has.
The university is awaiting the outcome of legal action which will determine the university's right to occupy the land and buildings at its Robina campus.
SEEN MY US WARSHIP?
The bad weather in the wake of Tropical Cyclone Justin has caused trouble in more ways than one...with an American military instructor losing his naval ship.
Instructor Frank Turkowski says it was quite a shock to fly all night to meet the USS Debuke and be unable to spot the ship when he got into Cairns on Monday morning.
Mr Turkowski says even the Australian Navy can't find the ship for him but he thinks it sailed to Darwin to avoid the cyclone.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
